mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized at -55.9% over the last four weeks with no deterioration trend. This floor signals commuting has reached a steady suppressed state. Retail-and-recreation will remain flat or decline slightly as the baseline of transit-dependent foot traffic is locked in at depressed levels.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not fallen below -56% in any of the four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points from its current -60.1% baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued at 16-17% above baseline across all four weeks, indicating sustained lockdown compliance and indoor preference. This behavioral lock-in suppresses retail-and-recreation demand as consumers remain home-bound despite stable grocery-pharmacy access, driving RETAIL_REC further negative.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained between 16.0% and 17.1% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 15% in any week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -55% in the next two weeks.

GROCERY_PHARM has declined from -25.7% to -27.3% over four weeks, signaling suppressed essential shopping. If holiday demand cannot overcome the grocery-pharmacy suppression signal, retail-and-recreation will fail to recover and decline further.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -27% while RETAIL_REC remains below -60%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 5 percentage points over the next four weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining suppressed below -25%.

Sustained workplace suppression prevents the return of commute-adjacent retail spending, locking RETAIL_REC into negative territory for the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -45% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has not risen above -46.9% in any of the four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility rises above -40% in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 percentage points from current baseline.

This outdoor preference may cannibalize indoor retail-and-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC more negative.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -47.9% to -38.0% between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -45% in both of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -58%.

This behavioral fragmentation prevents concentrated retail foot traffic, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES gap exceeds 8 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES converge within 5 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC rises above -57% in the next four weeks.

If this confidence extends to retail-and-recreation venues, RETAIL_REC will rise by 3-5 percentage points over the next four weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -34.1% to -27.3% over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -30% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 percentage points from current baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility at 16.4% and RETAIL_REC at -60.1% show inverse relationship. If RESIDENTIAL begins to decline below 16% (indicating policy relaxation or voluntary exit from home), RETAIL_REC will rise as consumers return to retail venues. This threshold-crossing signals regime shift from lockdown to reopening.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15.5% for one week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above 16% for all four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise by at least 2 percentage points within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL falling below 15.5%.
